title: Oldsmobile Cutlass Engines by Year (1961–1999)
description: Every factory engine in the Oldsmobile Cutlass, 442 and Cutlass Supreme by year, 1961–1999: the Jetfire turbo, the 400 and 455 W-30, Olds V8s and V6s.
intro: The Cutlass name ran on Oldsmobile's compact and mid-size cars from 1961 to 1999, and covered the 442, the Hurst/Olds and several later front-drive lines. The 442 began as an option package and was a separate model for 1968–1971; the trims column shows which engines it got.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The first F-85 and Cutlass used Oldsmobile's aluminum 215 V8, and the 1962–1963 Jetfire added a turbocharger.

From 1964 the Cutlass used Oldsmobile's cast-iron V8s: the 330, then the 350, with the 400 in the 442 and, from 1968, the 455. The W-30 package was the top 442 engine. Ratings are gross through 1971 and SAE net from 1972.
The Colonnade Cutlass carried SAE net ratings and Oldsmobile's 260, 350 and 455, with the 403 arriving for 1977.

The downsized rear-drive Cutlass Supreme, Salon, Calais and Cruiser used Buick V6s, Oldsmobile's 260, 307 and 350 V8s, and Oldsmobile diesels; the 1985–1987 4-4-2 used a 307. The front-drive Cutlass Ciera arrived in 1982 and the Cutlass Calais in 1985.
The front-drive Cutlass Supreme replaced the rear-drive car after 1988. The Ciera, Calais and the 1997–1999 Cutlass used GM fours and V6s, including Oldsmobile's Quad 4.

method: Every engine and year listed here was confirmed by at least three independent sources: the NHRA Stock Car Classification Guides, factory material such as GM Heritage Center information kits and sales brochures, EPA records and established references. Several Wikipedia articles count as one source. Where sources give different ratings, the factory figure is shown and the difference is noted. Factory race-only packages need two sources.
